title: Facebook Ads on a Budget: What £5–£50 a Day Gets You (UK)

facts.fact: Bons and Frazer's guide recommends a workable starting budget for a UK small business generating leads of £12-£25 a day, roughly £360-£750 a month.
facts.quote: a workable starting budget is **£12-£25 a day (roughly £360-£750 a month)**

facts.fact: Bons and Frazer states that below about £10 a day a small business can still get enquiries but costs swing week to week.
facts.quote: Below about £10 a day you can still get enquiries, but so few that costs swing week to week

facts.fact: Bons and Frazer's illustrative figures assume a cost per lead of around £20, which the guide says is in the range it commonly sees for UK local service businesses using lead forms.
facts.quote: assume a cost per lead of around **£20**, which is in the range we commonly see for UK local service businesses using lead forms

facts.fact: Bons and Frazer estimates that at a £20 cost per lead, about £140 a day (around £1,000 a week) is needed to reach Meta's roughly 50 conversions a week for exiting the learning phase on leads.
facts.quote: you’d need around £1,000 a week (roughly £140 a day) to hit Meta’s ~50 conversions a week

facts.fact: According to Bons and Frazer, Meta's own technical minimum is about $1 a day per ad set if charged per impression and about $5 a day if charged per click, like or video view.
facts.unit: USD per day per ad set
facts.quote: about **$1 a day per ad set** if you’re charged per impression, about **$5 a day** if you’re charged per click, like or video view

facts.fact: Bons and Frazer says Meta's minimum daily budget for rare events such as app installs or offer claims is around $40 a day.
facts.quote: around **$40 a day** for rare events like app installs or offer claims

facts.fact: Bons and Frazer gives a working minimum daily budget of £10-£12 per ad set for UK lead generation.
facts.unit: GBP per day per ad set
facts.quote: For lead generation, the working floor is nearer **£10-£12 a day**.

facts.fact: Bons and Frazer's rule of thumb is to spend at least half the expected cost per lead each day.
facts.value: half the expected cost per lead
facts.quote: spend at least half your expected cost per lead each day, so you average a lead every couple of days

facts.fact: Bons and Frazer states that Meta's minimum daily budget applies to each ad set separately.
facts.quote: The minimum applies to each ad set.

facts.fact: Bons and Frazer states that Facebook and Instagram ads are bought through the same Ads Manager and share one budget.
facts.quote: Facebook and Instagram ads are bought through the same Ads Manager and share one budget

facts.fact: Bons and Frazer states Meta has no minimum monthly spend, only a small daily floor per ad set.
facts.quote: Meta has no minimum monthly spend, only a small daily floor per ad set

facts.fact: Bons and Frazer describes a £5 a day budget as roughly £150 a month and expects 1-2 leads a week at a £20 cost per lead.
Bons and Frazer estimates a £12-£25 daily budget yields 4-8 leads a week at a £20 cost per lead.
Bons and Frazer estimates a £30-£50 daily budget yields 10-17 leads a week at a £20 cost per lead.
Bons and Frazer states that Meta's ad platform runs across Facebook, Instagram, Messenger and the Audience Network.
facts.quote: It's Meta's ad platform, running across Facebook, Instagram, Messenger and the Audience Network

facts.fact: Bons and Frazer says a daily budget is an average rather than a cap, so Meta can spend more on a strong day and less on a weak one.
facts.quote: A daily budget is an average, not a cap.

facts.fact: Meta has six campaign objectives in 2026: Awareness, Traffic, Engagement, Leads, App Promotion and Sales.
facts.quote: Meta has six campaign objectives in 2026: Awareness, Traffic, Engagement, Leads, App Promotion and Sales.

facts.fact: The page's suggested starting budget for a small Facebook ads test is £12-£25 a day (roughly £360-£750 a month), run for at least two weeks.
facts.quote: A practical starting point is £12-£25 a day (roughly £360-£750/month), run for at least two weeks.

facts.fact: The page says Meta's guidance is that an ad set usually needs around 50 optimisation events in the seven days after a significant edit to leave the learning phase.
facts.unit: optimisation events per ad set in 7 days
facts.quote: Meta’s guidance is that an ad set usually needs around 50 optimisation events in the seven days after a significant edit to leave the learning phase.

facts.fact: The page states Meta can spend up to 75% more than the daily budget on a high-opportunity day, provided the weekly total does not exceed seven times the daily budget.
facts.quote: Meta can spend up to 75% more than your daily budget on a high-opportunity day

facts.fact: The page says Meta raised its daily overspend allowance from 25% to 75%.
facts.quote: Meta raised this allowance from 25%, so older guides understate it.

facts.fact: The page advises raising a working campaign's budget by no more than 20-30% at a time to avoid returning it to the learning phase.
facts.quote: raise the budget by no more than 20-30% at a time

facts.fact: The page states the standalone Instagram Explore feed was retired in January 2026, with delivery moving into Reels.
facts.quote: the standalone Instagram Explore feed was

facts.fact: The page lists the recommended feed size for Facebook and Instagram feed ads as 1080×1350 (4:5) with 125 primary text characters and 40 headline characters.
The page lists the recommended Stories and Reels size as 1080×1920 (9:16), with text shown only in-video.
facts.quote: | Stories & Reels | 1080×1920 | 9:16 | In-video only |

facts.fact: The page lists carousel ads as 2-10 cards at 1080×1080 per card (1:1), with 125 primary and 40 headline characters per card.
facts.unit: pixels per card; 2-10 cards; 125 / 40 characters per card
facts.quote: | Carousel (2-10 cards) | 1080×1080 / card | 1:1 | 125 / 40 per card |

facts.fact: The page advises front-loading the message in the first 3 seconds of a video ad.
facts.quote: Front-load your message in the first 3 seconds and add captions

facts.fact: The page's worked example states that a roofer wanting 20 enquiries a month at a £25 cost per lead needs £500 a month, about £17 a day.
facts.quote: a roofer who wants 20 enquiries a month, at a £25 cost per lead, needs

facts.fact: In the page's roofer example, one in four enquiries becomes a job and the average job is worth £2,000.
facts.quote: If one in four enquiries becomes a job and the average job is worth £2,000

facts.fact: The page recommends running £12-£15 a day for three to four weeks to find your own cost per lead when it is unknown.
facts.quote: If you don’t know your cost per lead yet, run £12-£15 a day for three to four weeks and take the number from that.

facts.fact: The page gives the budget formula: monthly budget equals the number of leads wanted per month multiplied by the realistic cost per lead.
facts.quote: Monthly budget = leads you want a month × your realistic cost per lead

facts.fact: For a local trade business, the guide assumes 20 quote requests a month at a £25 cost per result, which means £500 monthly ad spend (about £17 a day).
facts.quote: | Local trade (roofer, loft boarder) | 20 quote requests | £25 | £500 | £17 |

facts.fact: For a private clinic or salon, the guide assumes 15 bookings a month at a £30 cost per result, which means £450 monthly ad spend (about £15 a day).
facts.quote: | Private clinic or salon | 15 bookings | £30 | £450 | £15 |

facts.fact: For a B2B service business, the guide assumes 8 qualified enquiries a month at a £60 cost per result, which means £480 monthly ad spend (about £16 a day).
facts.quote: | B2B service (accountant, consultant) | 8 qualified enquiries | £60 | £480 | £16 |

facts.fact: For an online shop, the guide assumes 40 orders a month at a £12 cost per result, which means £480 monthly ad spend (about £16 a day).
facts.quote: | Online shop | 40 orders | £12 | £480 | £16 |

facts.fact: At £10 a day with a £60 cost per lead, the guide says you would see about one enquiry a week.
facts.quote: At £10 a day and a £60 cost per lead, you’d see about one enquiry a week.

facts.fact: The guide's rule of thumb (its own, not a Meta rule) is not to call an ad a loser until it has spent two to three times the target cost per lead without a result.
facts.quote: don’t call an ad a loser until it has spent two to three times your target cost per lead without a result

facts.fact: The guide's rule of thumb (its own, not a Meta rule) is not to pick a winner between two ads until each has around ten results.
facts.quote: don’t pick a winner between two ads until each has around ten results.

facts.fact: The guide advises giving a new campaign 5-7 days before making meaningful changes.
facts.quote: Give a new campaign 5-7 days before making meaningful changes.

facts.fact: The guide advises reviewing campaigns every 5-7 days, longer on very small budgets.
facts.quote: Review properly every 5-7 days (longer on very small budgets)

facts.fact: The guide says that at £500 a month of ad spend, most professional management costs as much as the ads again, or more.
facts.quote: At £500 a month of ad spend, most professional management costs as much as the ads again, or more.

facts.fact: Meta's technical minimum daily budget per ad set is about $1 a day when charged per impression.
facts.unit: USD per day per ad set
facts.quote: Meta’s technical minimum is about $1 a day per ad set when you’re charged per impression

facts.fact: Meta's technical minimum daily budget per ad set is about $5 a day when charged per click, like or video view.
facts.unit: USD per day per ad set
facts.quote: about $5 a day when charged per click, like or video view

facts.fact: Meta's technical minimum daily budget per ad set is around $40 a day for rare events such as app installs.
facts.unit: USD per day per ad set
facts.quote: around $40 a day for rare events like app installs.

facts.fact: For lead generation, the guide recommends budgeting at least £10-£12 a day per ad set.
facts.unit: GBP per day per ad set
facts.quote: For lead generation, budget at least £10-£12 a day per ad set to get enough leads to judge your ads.

facts.fact: The guide gives a practical starting range of roughly £12-£25 a day (about £360-£750 a month), run for at least two weeks.
facts.quote: A practical start is roughly £12-£25 a day (about £360-£750/month), run for at least two weeks.

facts.fact: The guide states that below about £10 a day, results swing so much week to week that good and lucky ads cannot be told apart.
facts.quote: below about £10 a day results swing so much week to week that you can’t tell a good ad from a lucky one.

facts.fact: The guide says the learning phase needs roughly 50 conversions per ad set per week to stabilise.
facts.unit: conversions per ad set per week
facts.quote: The learning phase needs roughly 50 conversions per ad set per week to stabilise

facts.fact: The guide states that in 2026 Meta tightened attribution again, removing longer view-through windows and redefining what counts as a click.
facts.quote: in 2026 Meta tightened attribution again – removing longer view-through windows and redefining what counts as a click

facts.fact: The guide says a £20 lead where only half are genuine prospects is effectively a £40 lead.
facts.unit: GBP effective cost per qualified lead
facts.quote: A £20 lead where only half are genuine prospects is really a £40 lead.

facts.fact: A typical UK small-business budget on Facebook and Instagram ads is £360-£750 a month, which the page says is £12-£25 a day.
facts.quote: A typical UK small-business budget is £360-£750 a month on Facebook and Instagram ads, which is £12-£25 a day.

facts.fact: At a cost per lead of £20, a £600 monthly budget yields roughly 30 enquiries.
facts.quote: at £20 a lead, £600 a month is roughly 30 enquiries.

facts.fact: At a typical cost per lead of £20, a £5-a-day Facebook ads budget produces one or two enquiries a week.
facts.quote: At a typical £20 cost per lead, it’s one or two enquiries a week, with a lot of variation between weeks.

facts.fact: Meta wants around 50 results per ad set per week to finish its learning phase, according to the page.
facts.unit: results per ad set per week
facts.quote: Meta wants around 50 results per ad set per week to finish its learning phase.

facts.fact: Bons & Frazer sells Meta Ads management on a fixed monthly fee with server-side tracking built in and no contracts.
facts.quote: Bons & Frazer runs Meta Ads management for UK businesses on a fixed monthly fee, with server-side tracking built in.
